result.title: Analyzing the Dynamics of WSBM-based Echo State Networks using InputDSA
result.comment: 9 pages excluding refs and appendices, 9 figures
result.summary: Bridging the structural gap between biological brains and artificial neural networks presents a pathway to altered computational dynamics. This paper introduces a Reservoir Computing framework that replaces random networks with biologically realistic modularity by applying the Weighted Stochastic Block Model (WSBM) to Echo State Networks (ESNs). This topological parameterization constructs reservoirs reflecting latent functional sub-circuits. Furthermore, the integration of Input Dynamical Similarity Analysis (InputDSA) provides a mechanism to isolate and compare how structural priors modulate intrinsic recurrent dynamics versus external inputs. By evaluating these architectures, we establish that structural diversity does not necessarily predicts behavioral diversity across the selected network subset. Furthermore, our demixed analysis confirms Anna Karenina principle of dynamics, demonstrating that environmental constraints enforce dynamical convergence in successful agents, while failing networks degenerate into idiosyncratic trajectories.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用 Weighted Stochastic Block Model 替换随机连接以构造具生物模块性的 Echo State Network 储层，并引入 InputDSA 分离结构先验对内在递归动力学与外部输入的影响，发现结构多样性不必然带来行为多样性、且成功网络在环境约束下动力学趋于收敛。
AI.relevance_reason: InputDSA 可分离「内在递归状态动力学」与「外部输入驱动」的贡献，可供核查是否迁移用于拆分 VLM 推理中视觉证据输入与 latent 推理状态的贡献；其模块化功能子回路设置也提示与推理工作区/子回路假设的可能联系，但均属推测。
